A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same masked-diffusion convergence analysis. Their complete text, equations, proofs and figures support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix; the proofs appear in Section 4.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs and discussion, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 adds original Monte Carlo experiments on a synthetic Potts chain in Section 5, with sampling-error results plotted in Figure 1.

M1.justification: The factorized predictor, training objective and uniform-unmasking sampler in Equations (4)–(6) remain unchanged. New Remark 1 additionally specifies an untested sampling heuristic: estimate conditional entropies and reveal the lowest-entropy masked positions first.

E1.justification: V1 has no empirically evaluated dataset. V2 introduces synthetic sequence-generation evaluation using a K-state Potts chain, with K = 10 and sequence length L = 100. This establishes the paper's first empirical coverage, without adding natural-language benchmarks.

E2.justification: The analytical comparisons with prior convergence guarantees are retained. V2's Figure 1 evaluates only the analyzed sampler; no competing sampler or autoregressive baseline is experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 introduces the first evaluation protocol: an exact conditional predictor, equal numbers of unmasked tokens per iteration, and expected KL divergence estimated over masks and data. It varies iteration count T at J = 2 and varies coupling J at T = 10. These are new experiments, not revisions to earlier settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds two controlled sensitivity analyses absent from v1: sampling error versus iteration count and sampling error versus token dependence, controlled through the Potts coupling. Figure 1 directly tests both central scaling predictions of the theory.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports Monte Carlo estimation of the KL expectation over mask randomness and the data distribution. It supplies no simulation counts, seeds, error bars or confidence intervals, so the addition concerns estimation methodology rather than quantified uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figure 1 introduces the paper's first numerical results: a reported log-log slope near -1 for error versus T and approximately linear error growth with summed token mutual information. V1 contains the corresponding theoretical predictions but no numerical observations.

T1.justification: V2 specifies previously unspecified constants: C1 = T s_max / sum_t s_t in Corollary 1, and coefficients s_max/(2L) and s_max/(16L) in Theorem 2. The principal assumptions, asymptotic rates and Section 4 proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The new title, abstract and contribution paragraph explicitly claim that high-quality sampling with T < L breaks AR's L-step sampling bottleneck. V1 foregrounded general convergence guarantees and tightness. The underlying mutual-information-dependent convergence contribution is retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive qualification that practical diffusion implementations are typically slower than optimized AR models with KV caching. Remark 1 supplies an entropy-based interpretation for choosing unmasking positions, and the discussion adds low-order Markov structure as a possible route to lower error.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly documents the synthetic generator's initial distribution and transition probabilities, numerical parameters, exact predictor and balanced schedule. These support reproducing the simulation design, although code, hardware, Monte Carlo sample counts and seeds are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds six cited works, including Pope et al. on inference efficiency and Deschenaux and Gulcehre and Hayakawa et al. on distillation. These expand practical positioning, while the related-work taxonomy and principal theoretical comparisons remain intact.

P1.justification: The title and portions of the abstract and introduction are revised, a numerical-experiments section precedes the renumbered discussion, and a remark and explanatory footnote are added. Most existing exposition and the proof organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel Figure 1, showing error versus iterations on logarithmic axes and error versus mutual information on linear axes. Equation (11) is reformatted and pagination shifts, including the contents spilling onto page 2; the overall single-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 provide useful numerical corroboration of both central scaling predictions, while the new runtime caveat makes the practical discussion more precise. The gains are limited: the proofs are largely unchanged, validation uses one synthetic distribution with an exact predictor, and Monte Carlo uncertainty is unreported. The experiments also do not establish the practical acceleration emphasized by the new title.
